caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 765 of 1998.
lawyer:
Fazlul Karim Senior Advocate instructed by Md Nawab Ali Advocate-on-Record------For the Petitioners. 
Mahmudul Islam, Senior Advocate instructed by Sufia Khatun, Advocate-on-Record------For Respondent Nos.2. 3. 5. 9 & 10.
Not represented-Respondent Nos. 1, 4, 6-8, 11-24.

Nurul Islam and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Jamila Khatun and others ------ Respondents.
full_judgment:
Kazi Ebadul Hoque J: Defendant-petitioners seek leave to appeal from judgment-and decree of the Division Bench of the High Court Division dated 27-5-1998 passed in First Appeal No.33 of 1990 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 30-9-1989 passed by the Subordinate Judge, First Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.339 of 1977. 

 3. Defendant Nos. 3 and 4, defendant No. 11 and defendant Nos. 13-18 contested the suit by filing 3 separate written statements. Case of defendant Nos.3 and 4 is that Matilal Podder obtained a decree against Ashutosh Das in Money Suit No. 39 of 1955 and put the decree into execution in Money Execution Case No.19 of 1959 and sold the suit property in auction and one Rahema Begum purchased the same and took delivery of possession on 26-1-1961. Thereafter she sold the same to defendant Nos. 3 and 4 by a registered sale deed and delivered the possession of the same to the defendants. Case of defendant No.11 is that he alone purchased the suit property from Rahema Begum by 6(six) registered sale deeds in his own name and in the names of his friends. Case of defendant Nos. 13-18 are that they along with some other members of their families purchased the suit property from defendant Nos. 3 and 4. 

 4. Trial Court decreed the suit by judgment and decree dated 30-9-1989. Title Suit No.633 of 1982 was also transferred to the First Court of Subordinate Judge and renumbered as Title Suit No.109 of 1983 and the same was also heard analogously with Title Suit No.339 of 1977 and decreed by the aforesaid judgment dated 30-9-1989. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.339 of 1977 petitioners along with two others preferred First Appeal No.33 of 1990 which was dismissed by the impugned judgment. Being aggrieved by the same petitioners seek leave to appeal. 

 5. Learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that in view of the provisions of section 213(1) of the Succession Act 1925 plaintiff having not produced probate of the will executed by Noni Gopal Das in favour of Joy Gopal Das mere assertion in the plaint that Joy Gopal Das obtained a probate was not sufficient to hold that Joy Gopal Das became the 16 annas owner of the suit property and his heirs defendant Nos. 1 and 2 had right to sell the entire suit property and, as such, High Court Division acted illegally in affirming the judgment and decree of the trial Court. He further submits that from the facts and circumstances of the case it appears that defendant Nos. 1 and 2 were coerced to enter into the disputed contract for sale and, as such, trial Court acted illegally in exercise of its discretion to pass a decree for specific performance of contract in favour of the plaintiff and High Court Division acted illegally in not interfering with the same. He further submits that the petitioners not being party to the contract or privy of the contracting parties and having not purchased suit property from the vendors subsequent to the deed of agreement with a notice of the same the suit against them was not maintainable and trial Court acted Illegally in passing the decree and the High Court Division acted illegally in affirming the same. In support of his last contention learned Advocate relied on the decision in the case of Prem Sukh Gulgulia vs Habib Ullah reported in AIR 1945 Calcutta 355 and the case of Golam Kader vs Abdul Khaleque Choukder reported in 43 DLR (AD) 107. 

 7. High Court Division considered the aforesaid decisions relied on by the learned Advocate for the petitioners and also considered some other decisions and held that the suit for specific performance of contract against defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and recovery of possession against the other defendants is maintainable and defendants other than defendant Nos. 1 and 2, are necessary parties. We find no illegality in the aforesaid finding of the High Court Division to disagree with the same. In a suit for specific performance of a contract for sale of immoveable property plaintiff is entitled to delivery of possession in the suit property after execution and registration of the deed of sale in his favour in execution of the decree eventually passed in his favour. Such relief cannot be frustrated by a trespasser and, as such, a trespasser in the suit property is liable to be impleaded in the suit and evicted from the suit property to give effective relief to the plaintiff.
